description: Two separate frozen synthetic corpora from the model comparison. No real personal memories. See docs/embedding-model.md.

corpora.description: Hand-authored synthetic memory retrieval diagnostic; frozen before model scoring. Not production data or a general model leaderboard.

documents.text: Repository uses Bun to install JavaScript dependencies; npm is not supported for this project.
Encrypted database backups run every Tuesday at 02:00 and are retained for thirty days.
The memory service listens only on loopback; remote access must pass through the private VPN.
The mobile app forces dark mode, but desktop appearance follows the operating system theme.
Search combines FTS5 keyword results with cosine similarity over normalized embeddings.
If model inference fails, the service returns keyword search results after a short timeout.
A successful restore drill is required before deleting any older backup snapshots.
Use semantic HTML controls so keyboard users can reach every action.

documents.title: Package restoration
documents.text: Restore JavaScript packages with pnpm using the checked-in lockfile. Adding a new dependency requires owner approval.

documents.title: Canonical instructions
documents.text: Keep one canonical AGENTS.md shared by all coding assistants. Do not create separate Claude or Cursor instruction files.

documents.title: Synthetic database tests
documents.text: Run experiments against fabricated records or an isolated database copy. Never test deletes against the authoritative memory database.

documents.title: Reboot permission
documents.text: Rebooting or shutting down the shared machine requires explicit approval from its owner, even when an update recommends it.

documents.title: Local process restart
documents.text: The assistant may stop and restart a temporary development server it started for the current task. Shared background services need owner approval.

documents.title: Backup retention
documents.text: Keep daily encrypted snapshots for fourteen days. Keep monthly encrypted snapshots for one year.

documents.title: Backup schedule
documents.text: The synthetic memory backup job starts at 03:15 UTC every day. The nightly report email is sent at 04:00 UTC.

documents.title: Restore verification
documents.text: Backup success means a consistent snapshot was restored and queried successfully. Merely seeing a backup file does not prove recoverability.

documents.title: Restore rehearsal
documents.text: A restore drill must run before any older snapshots are pruned. Rehearse using an isolated destination so the live store remains available.

documents.title: SQLite consistency
documents.text: Use SQLite VACUUM INTO for a consistent snapshot while WAL is active. Copying only memory.db can omit recent committed transactions.

documents.title: Temporary snapshot permissions
documents.text: Create a private temporary snapshot with mode 0600 and keep that mode throughout copying. Changing permissions after completion leaves an exposure window.

documents.title: No-overwrite publication
documents.text: Publishing a backup must fail when the destination exists. It must never replace an earlier recovery file with the same name.

documents.title: Private listener
documents.text: The memory API binds to 127.0.0.1. Another device reaches it through the approved private VPN route.

documents.title: Public setup
documents.text: The public website provides installation instructions and a setup form. Memory tools and device approval pages stay on the private authenticated endpoint.

documents.title: Stateless clients
documents.text: Agent clients forward requests to one authenticated memory server. They do not maintain writable local memory databases.

documents.title: Five tools
documents.text: The remote memory API supports context, store, search, get, and archive. It cannot crawl or index files on the server.

documents.title: Unresolved project identity
documents.text: Without a durable project ID or a sanitized Git remote, project identity is unresolved. Do not silently treat project-specific information as global.

documents.title: Credential-free project ID
documents.text: A project key is id:<durable-id> or git:<host/repository>. Strip URL credentials and query parameters; filesystem paths are not stable project identities.

documents.title: Device scope
documents.text: A keyboard mapping for fixture-mac belongs to the device scope. A preference intended for every machine belongs to explicit global scope.

documents.title: OS scope
documents.text: Operating-system memory uses macos, windows, or linux. Darwin and win32 are not valid platform labels.

documents.title: Expected revision conflict
documents.text: A correction must include the current expected revision. On revision_conflict, read the latest record, reconcile, and submit a new correction.

documents.title: Uncertain write replay
documents.text: If a save times out, retry only with the same request ID and exactly the same payload. A changed payload requires a new logical request.

documents.title: Save acknowledgement
documents.text: An acknowledged memory ID and revision prove the save. Do not fetch the record again routinely just to verify an acknowledged write.

documents.title: History preservation
documents.text: Correcting a memory creates a new revision. Earlier contents remain inspectable; restoring an older version also creates a new revision.

documents.title: Confirmed preferences
documents.text: Only explicit user statements or accepted decisions can be confirmed. An observation from a tool cannot replace a confirmed preference with unconfirmed content.

documents.title: Reversible archive
documents.text: Archiving hides a record from ordinary context and search but preserves revision history. An authorized unarchive restores visibility.

documents.title: Immediate searchability
documents.text: A newly stored memory is searchable immediately. There is no overnight batch job or delayed vector indexing stage.

documents.title: Keyword fallback
documents.text: When embedding inference fails, return lexical FTS results and report semantic recall as unavailable. Do not claim that the vector path succeeded.

documents.title: Context ordering
documents.text: Startup context prioritizes confirmed preferences, then accepted decisions, handoffs, and other knowledge. Newness alone does not displace a stable preference.

documents.title: Omission bookkeeping
documents.text: When context exceeds its byte budget, return omission counts plus omitted record IDs and revisions. Never present a partial excerpt as a full record.

documents.title: Missing token
documents.text: Requests without a valid bearer token are rejected before tool dispatch. A missing token gets HTTP 401.

documents.title: Device revocation
documents.text: Revoking a device credential prevents later memory requests from that client. Other approved devices retain their independent credentials.

documents.title: One editor
documents.text: Only one assistant may edit a checkout at a time. A second assistant can review read-only or work in a separate authorized worktree.

documents.title: Narrow Git staging
documents.text: Stage only the files changed for the current outcome. Preserve unrelated uncommitted work and avoid blanket git add when a checkout is dirty.

documents.title: Delivery evidence
documents.text: Local commits, pushed commits, installed releases, and deployed behavior are distinct states. Verify each delivery step actually reached its destination.

documents.title: Unit test evidence
documents.text: A passing unit suite proves its covered local contracts. It does not prove authenticated desktop integration or behavior on another operating system.

documents.title: Native controls
documents.text: Use semantic HTML buttons and inputs with labels. Keyboard users must be able to reach and operate every action.

documents.title: Appearance preference
documents.text: The synthetic phone app uses dark appearance. The desktop app follows the operating system appearance.

documents.title: Error diagnosis
documents.text: The fixture exporter fails with E_LOCKED when another writer holds its output directory lock. Wait for the owning exporter; do not delete its lock while it is running.

documents.title: Environment switch
documents.text: Set FIXTURE_MODEL_ROOT to the model directory for real inference tests. An unset value skips those tests and is not a real-model pass.

documents.title: Snapshot symbol
documents.text: PublishSnapshotNoReplace publishes a private snapshot without replacing an existing destination. CopySnapshotOverwrite is a retired unsafe helper name.

documents.title: Vector compatibility
documents.text: Vectors are filtered by exact embedding_model identity and compatible dimensions. Equal dimensions do not make vectors from different models interchangeable.

documents.title: Model migration
documents.text: Change models through a verified snapshot and shadow re-embedding. Preserve IDs, scopes, revisions, old binaries, and a tested rollback before a cutover.

documents.title: No database mining
documents.text: Save explicit preferences and verified handoffs selectively. Do not mine private chat transcripts to populate the memory service.

documents.title: Fresh-session acceptance
documents.text: To verify startup context, start a fresh authenticated agent session and inspect the returned memory. Reusing a running session may preserve old context.

documents.title: Wrong pending options
documents.text: Validate incompatible connection options before requesting device approval. A corrected retry should recover from pending setup without another approval cycle.

documents.title: Polling ownership
documents.text: A device-approval viewer allows one refresh in flight and owns one follow-up timer. Older responses cannot overwrite newer approval state.

documents.title: Quoted executable paths
documents.text: An agent hook command must recognize executable paths containing spaces and apostrophes. Reinstalling the hook should not leave duplicate entries.

corpora.description: Second synthetic corpus: preferences and unrelated product outcomes. Fixed before its model runs; no real personal or production memory.

documents.title: Coffee choice
documents.text: In the invented household, Dana drinks decaffeinated coffee with oat milk after lunch. Morgan drinks black tea with dairy milk.

documents.title: Meeting window
documents.text: Dana prefers meetings after 13:00 local time because mornings are reserved for uninterrupted writing. Early appointments are acceptable only for emergencies.

documents.title: Reading format
documents.text: For technical manuals Dana prefers searchable PDF files. For fiction Dana prefers printed paperback books and avoids reading novels on a tablet.

documents.title: Music queue
documents.text: The synthetic music player starts an instrumental jazz queue during focused work. Spoken podcasts are reserved for walks and must not enter the work queue.

documents.title: Notification rule
documents.text: Only overdue deadlines should create an audible notification. Routine activity updates remain silent but appear in the activity list.

documents.title: Travel preference
documents.text: Dana chooses direct train journeys over flights for trips shorter than four hours. Longer journeys may use a nonstop flight.

documents.title: Book list limit
documents.text: The Arcadia reading app shows at most five next books. Finished books belong in history and do not occupy a next-book slot.

documents.title: Rain unit
documents.text: The Nimbus garden display reports precipitation in millimeters. Indoor room temperature uses degrees Celsius, and air pressure uses hectopascals.

documents.title: Artwork cadence
documents.text: The Canvas display changes its featured painting at 07:00 local time daily. The weather panel refreshes every fifteen minutes.

documents.title: Paused timer
documents.text: Pausing a session timer preserves elapsed time. Reset clears the elapsed duration. Resuming a paused session continues from the saved duration.

documents.title: Duplicate library items
documents.text: The Cedar library app identifies duplicate books by ISBN plus edition. Different editions of the same title remain separate items.

documents.title: Invitation recovery
documents.text: An invitation link expires after ten minutes. An expired link offers a fresh invitation without losing the draft collaborator list.

documents.title: API decision
documents.text: The Cedar catalog uses REST endpoints rather than GraphQL because it has two simple clients and stable request shapes. Revisit the decision only if query flexibility becomes a proven problem.

documents.title: Storage decision
documents.text: The Pocket prototype uses one SQLite database because it runs on a single host. The analytics warehouse is a separate PostgreSQL service.

documents.title: Release acceptance
documents.text: A synthetic photo export is acceptable only when the album order and original capture dates survive. Pixel-perfect thumbnail appearance is outside acceptance.

documents.title: Draft visibility
documents.text: The Draftdesk preview can be shared through an expiring signed link. The unpublished draft must not appear in the public directory until the owner publishes it.

documents.title: Cache decision
documents.text: The Leaf reader caches downloaded articles for offline reading. It does not cache authenticated account responses because another person may use the same device.

documents.title: Search preference
documents.text: The Cedar catalog sorts exact title matches before approximate matches. Popularity is a tie-breaker only among results with equal relevance.

documents.title: Accent regression
documents.text: The Leaf search bug came from stripping accents on stored titles but not on queries. Normalize both paths consistently so cafe finds café.

documents.title: Badge regression
documents.text: The Nimbus unread badge stayed visible because the mark-read handler failed to persist the acknowledged event ID. Save that ID before recalculating the badge.

documents.title: Export line endings
documents.text: The Cedar exporter must write CRLF line endings for the legacy Windows importer. UTF-8 content stays unchanged; replacing accented letters is not part of the fix.

documents.title: Rotation function
documents.text: RotateFeaturedArt selects the next painting once per day. RefreshForecast only updates weather data and must never advance the art queue.

documents.title: Timeout error
documents.text: The Arcadia sync client reports E_REMOTE_TIMEOUT after a fifteen-second response deadline. Retry reads with bounded backoff; never delete the local draft after that error.

documents.title: Test root variable
documents.text: Set CATALOG_FIXTURE_ROOT to fabricated sample files for exporter acceptance tests. USER_LIBRARY_ROOT refers to the real library and must not be used for destructive trials.

documents.title: Coffee grinder
documents.text: The coffee grinder burrs need cleaning every second Sunday. Tea bags belong in a separate pantry drawer.

documents.title: Transit tickets
documents.text: A regional train ticket can be refunded until midnight before departure. Flight vouchers expire in twelve months.

documents.title: Book covers
documents.text: Arcadia loads cover thumbnails from its image cache. A missing cover uses a text label with the book title.

documents.title: Weather source
documents.text: Nimbus reads weather observations from the station sensor and forecasts from a remote provider.

documents.title: Frames
documents.text: Canvas supports a black frame and a wooden frame. Frame choice does not change the painting dimensions.

documents.title: Timer colors
documents.text: The session timer uses green while running and amber when paused. The elapsed-time font remains readable in both states.

documents.title: Catalog storage
documents.text: Cedar stores cover images outside the catalog database and includes their checksums in an export manifest.

documents.title: Invite permissions
documents.text: A collaborator who accepts an invitation receives read access to published albums but cannot publish the owner’s drafts.

documents.title: Archive formats
documents.text: The photo exporter produces a ZIP archive containing one image per capture plus a JSON manifest.

documents.title: Reader browser
documents.text: Leaf opens external links in the system browser. A downloaded article can still be read without connectivity.

documents.title: Notification history
documents.text: Nimbus activity history records device check-ins and successful forecast refreshes, including timestamps.

documents.title: Sync schedule
documents.text: Arcadia sends background sync reads every five minutes while online and suspends them when disconnected.

documents.text: For technical manuals Dana prefers searchable PDF files. For fiction Dana prefers printed paperback books and avoids reading novels on a tablet.

documents.title: Music queue
documents.text: The synthetic music player starts an instrumental jazz queue during focused work. Spoken podcasts are reserved for walks and must not enter the work queue.

documents.title: Notification rule archived
documents.text: Only overdue deadlines should create an audible notification. Routine activity updates remain silent but appear in the activity list.

documents.title: Travel preference archived
documents.text: Dana chooses direct train journeys over flights for trips shorter than four hours. Longer journeys may use a nonstop flight.

documents.title: Book list limit archived
documents.text: The Arcadia reading app shows at most five next books. Finished books belong in history and do not occupy a next-book slot.

documents.title: Rain unit archived
documents.text: The Nimbus garden display reports precipitation in millimeters. Indoor room temperature uses degrees Celsius, and air pressure uses hectopascals.
